inputs.text: Support-programme workers at the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth are being asked to rely on government assurances while their livelihoods remain unprotected by law. Their protest outside the Presidential Palace and 24-hour strike show the imbalance of power: workers bear the risk, while the government can leave its promises unenforceable. If officials claim they have met the workers’ main demands, they should put that commitment into legally binding guarantees of job security. Rights at work should not depend on trust alone.
